title: Rehearsals and hours at the Onyx Club
summary: Rehearsals were afternoon; music ran from eight or nine until two-thirty; sit-ins happened at Jimmy Ryan's next door.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Just string bass. Was it that Kirby sort of let the band members do what they wanted to do as far as the kind of back-up that the band members wanted you to give them as a drummer?
Whatever they wanted was all right with him, in other words. I see. How about rehearsing with Kirby? What did he do as far as rehearsing is concerned?
Well, we had a... We rehearsed sometimes once a week down in the Onyx Club.

Afternoons. And he'd make it earlier because people started coming in down there. We'd always get down there I'd say about three(?) and twelve... About two hours. Because people started coming in, you know, for lunch hour. The bar was open about that time, you know...
But what time did the music start? What time was it scheduled to start at the Onyx Club?

And we was there... We didn't start sometimes until about 8:30, sometimes nine o'clock, waiting until the people started coming in, you know. Because we'd go until 2:30, sometimes 3 o'clock. Small place. A very good place to play in. The Onyx Club was something like the Three Deuces. It was right side of Jimmy Ryan's, right next door to Jimmy Ryan's -- both of them right together there. And a lot of different musicians from different places; different musicians stopped in at the Onyx Club. We didn't have too much sit in, sitting-in, not in John Kirby's band at the Onyx Club. All them sit-ins used to happen next door at Jimmy Ryan's, playing a lot of Dixieland stuff.
